name: Chikkamagaluru
headline: Migrant plantation families keep children out of school each pepper and coffee harvest.
summary: Each harvest season families migrate into Chikkamagaluru to work in coffee and pepper plantations, and children live in roadside tents minding younger siblings instead of attending school. A school in Begar made four regular students write SSLC as private candidates without parental consent, and parents threatened to withdraw daughters over the 2022 hijab ban.

reasons.detail: Hundreds of migrant families work the coffee and pepper harvest; their children miss school while living in makeshift tents.
Karnataka Public School Begar allegedly registered four regular students as private candidates without parental consent, costing them internal marks.

reasons.factor: Forest-hamlet tribal families and school access
reasons.detail: Forest communities near Ajjampura relied on ashrama schools; during Covid closures there was no network in forests and limited support. The article says such schools offer classes only up to Class 7 (state-wide statement).
Parents said they would withdraw daughters from high schools if headscarves were barred during the 2022 row.

reasons.factor: Cheap child labour in poor families
reasons.detail: The 2021 report quotes that child labour is cheap and easily employed among first-generation Adivasi learners, pushing children towards work instead of school; Chikkamagaluru communities feature among its examples.

Teachers found malnad students, a majority from Shivamogga, Uttara Kannada and Chikkamagaluru, skipping college for Bengaluru catering jobs paying Rs 1,000 a day; increase noted after Covid. College-level evidence.

reasons.factor: Government school teacher and facility gaps
reasons.detail: Coverage around the child rights commission's dropout count notes that government schools in Chikkamagaluru lack teachers and basic facilities, with calls for more appointments.

headlines.title: Education rights adalat made mandatory
headlines.takeaway: Child rights commission counted 102 dropouts in Chikkamagaluru and launched Shaale Kade Nanna Nade to readmit them.

responses.text: The Shaale Kade Nanna Nade campaign was organised to readmit school dropouts, planned as a mass movement, with identification of dropouts elsewhere in the district continuing.
